test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 3 hours and 36 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 4 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill two-third of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the taps be **A**, **B**, and **C** (emptying tap).

Combined efficiency = 12 + 1 − 9 = 4 units/hour (Total Work = 36 units).

Work to be done = 2/3 × 36 = 24 units.

Time required = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling Tap 1 (A) = 3 hours, Filling Tap 2 (B) = 36 hours, Emptying Tap 3 (C) = 4 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of individual times; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

⇒ Net efficiency of all taps = 12 + 1 − 9 = 4 units/hour.

⇒ Target capacity to fill = 2/3 × Total Work = 2/3 × 36 = 24 units.

⇒ Time taken = Target Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Taps

Inlet taps perform **positive work** (filling), while outlet/leakage taps perform **negative work** (emptying) relative to the cistern capacity.

Work and Time Relation

Time is **inversely proportional** to efficiency. If a tap fills a tank in 'x' hours, its 1-hour work is 1/x of the total capacity.

Net Efficiency Formula

For two inlets (a, b) and one outlet (c), the net work done in one hour is (1/a + 1/b − 1/c).</p
